notes: Site: IKEA UAE (ikea.com/ae/en), sibling of IKEA UK (SR92)/DE (SR107)/FR (SR140), all of which found New Arrivals at the same base path shape /new/new-products/. Probed /ae/en/cat/new-products/, /new-arrivals/, /new-in/ etc. first - all 301-redirected to the generic catalog-root fallback /cat/products-products/ (i.e. not valid distinct slugs on this market's /cat/ tree). Following the sibling URL shape instead, https://www.ikea.com/ae/en/new/new-products/ returned HTTP 200 directly via tier-1 HTTP fetch (no Playwright needed - count present in SSR payload). Page H1 'New products', <title> 'Find New Furniture, Decor & More Online in UAE - IKEA', meta description 'Discover the latest arrivals at IKEA UAE. Shop new furniture, decor, and more with UAE Online Shopping. Explore what's new and refresh your home.' - a genuine 'recently added to catalogue' merchandising concept with a real browsable/filterable product grid, matching the UK/DE/FR siblings' classification exactly. Department chips inspected directly (e.g. https://www.ikea.com/ae/en/new/new-products/?filters=f-availability:ONLINE_SELLABLE,f-subcategories:kt001) and confirmed as query-param filters of the SAME base /new/new-products/ listing, not distinct site-curated New Arrivals sub-pages - no sub-categories invented. SSR HTML shows '1231 items' (filter-panel header) and 'Showing 24 of 1231 results' with progress max=1231 (results-list footer) - both consistent. Also found three '/new/<slug>-pub<id>/' editorial landing pages linked from the homepage (e.g. 'let-your-home-come-out-and-play', 'meet-the-ikea-ps-2026-collection', 'the-art-of-making-art-affordable') - opened one representative page ('let-your-home-come-out-and-play'): this is a themed marketing/editorial article (campaign copy, no total-count element) that links onward to one named themed collection category (grejsimojs-collection-700709), not itself a New Arrivals PLP - excluded per the 'New Collection'/editorial-landing-page exclusion rule in Sec.3, not flagged ambiguous since it has no product-count/PLP shape of its own (pure editorial article). No other New Arrivals-labelled entry point found via candidate slug probing or homepage link scan. Did not need Claude-in-Chrome (tier 3).
